author: Codex critical design seat /root/design91_option_rule
scope: Design, primary-source review and hand schedule only. No model, RTL, Linux, build or board execution.
name: SET-WRITE withdrawal certificate: end a no-longer-needed destination walk when another admissible output has a real lease
decision: Keep as a bounded mechanism hypothesis and safe fallback for root's prefix-retarget direction. Bare cancellation, priority, hot-first and matching are not contributions. A known interruptible-prefetch mechanism exactly reproduces the early-A case. The remaining distinction is a cross-address COPY semantic withdrawal event before any concrete X AW, not an improved generic cancel primitive.

problem.scene: Three legal 64B COPYs form the example. Historical A1 wrote Y, its consumer reads it and later releases Y. V has already performed its necessary normal READ and accepts X or Y in one registered output class. X is FREE but cold; Y is initially consumer-owned but resident. Another DMA A2 later needs a fixed output Z and a cold source. The ownership relationship is actual producer/consumer use of one page, not invented shared-payload triangles.
problem.missing_action: Ordinary late allocation can bind V to Y once Y is FREE. N may already let that hit pass while a cold-X preparation walk runs. It therefore need not improve V's permission latency. The actionable residual is stopping cold-X PTEs that no legal COPY will use after V chooses Y.
problem.predicate_scope: Each parent has an immutable accepted-slot bitmap within a registered pool/class plus its full context/options. A FREE slot is only usable if its bit is set, length/offset fit, its registered lease class matches and its own WRITE receives normal permission checks. Initial proof scope uses stable pinned single-stage 4KiB mappings and common legal cache keys for the shared pool. Different contexts do not share grants or hotness merely because PA is equal.
problem.ordinary_matching_boundary: Matching can choose Y and exchange X/Y leases exactly. It cannot by itself remove already-started X translation work; adding the complete withdrawal wire and cancel contract is an equivalent implementation of this proposal, not a separate heuristic it must beat. A published generic interruptible prepare already covers cancellation on higher-priority tablewalk arrival, which is a concrete executable strong control.

proposed_action.interface: COPY_TO_SET(src,pool,accepted_mask,length,tag,context/options) is immutable from its first VALID. Its implementation may use an internal nonarchitectural PREPARE(X) command. It has not emitted a concrete X AXI AW, an ordinary fixed-X upstream AW or a WRITE data transaction.
proposed_action.anchor: After normal source READ succeeds, choose a FREE fallback anchor X and reserve its actual slot lease. Launch at most one optional prepare walk. X guarantees a valid fallback output if no other slot releases; selection is ordinary RR, not a new matching algorithm.
proposed_action.withdrawal_witness: Before any concrete destination AW, atomically acquire a genuinely FREE, accepted Y and release X. Freeze Y in the new actual WRITE child and poison X's internal preparation ticket. The immutable parent still denotes the same set; no published concrete address changes. Lease acquisition means ownership only, not permission. Y still runs its own normal context/WRITE checks and actual AW/W/B.
proposed_action.walk_rule: If X preparation is still active, issue cancel(ticket,epoch). Never withdraw an already visible AR VALID. If a PTE AR is visible, retain its fields until READY, then drain its R response. At the next response boundary suppress only future unpublished PTE ARs, X's fill and the X-prepare terminal error/result, then acknowledge cancellation and release its pending lifecycle. If no AR has yet become visible, it may terminate immediately.
proposed_action.bound: At most one output swap per parent. A stale resident hint may lead to a normal Y miss or error but cannot authorize a write. Once concrete Y WRITE is published it stays fixed and follows normal fault completion; no silent X fallback after a public Y AW. Source payload remains charged and retained until genuine WRITE completion/error drain.
proposed_action.new_information: Registered accepted-set/class identity, an atomic real lease-exchange result, the optional prepare's ticket/epoch and irreversible-publication state. No future consumer release prediction, PA grant reuse or arbitrary mid-VALID request rewrite is assumed.

pseudocode: on accept SET parent: latch source,set,context,length,tag; reserve ordinary payload and completion space; execute real normal source READ
on READ_DONE(success): reserve one FREE accepted anchor X; issue PREPARE(X, optional=1, ticket,epoch); state=OPTION

on actual release(Y): if state==OPTION and switches_left and accepted(Y) and FREE(Y) and advisory_resident(Y): atomically lease(Y), release(X), freeze concrete Y child; switches_left=0; poison X ticket; request CANCEL_X; state=CHOSEN
on X_PREPARE_DONE while state==OPTION: retain X lease and freeze X child; actual WRITE uses normal IOMMU permissions; an efficient legitimate prepare-ticket control is separately allowed
on X_PREPARE_DONE while ticket poisoned: discard result; do not generate X WRITE; do not count VALID as grant
PTW on cancel_pending: if current AR was already first-VALID, hold/drain it; after its response suppress next unpublished AR/fill and return CANCELLED(ticket,epoch)
on concrete chosen WRITE: normal checks; stable AW, all W, final B, completion after cache synchronization; consumer owns output until validated release
on any parent error: legally drain actual transactions, quarantine bound output when required, return terminal error; complete fault recovery is required new implementation work

contracts.permission: X preparation cannot be interpreted as permission for Y. No per-SID/DC grant sharing. Y gets normal access checking using its own actual chosen request. Fixed stable mappings make the first prototype small; remapping/revocation/error replay are not declared solved.
contracts.axi: The critical cutoff is first VALID, including VALID&&!READY, not acceptance alone. Cancel at PROC_PTE must win before the next MEM_ACCESS publishes AR. Existing fixed-destination burst_req_t stays unchanged.
contracts.ordering: The kernel publishes an accepted class/bitmap before enqueue, owns lease generations, orders consumer access/cache synchronization before release, and serializes release/lease exchange. Reconfiguration requires full drain. Completion slot was reserved before READ so full CQ cannot trap an issued B.
contracts.fairness: One swap and one prepare per parent; age priority for actual demands; low-priority optional preparation. If no eligible new slot appears, complete X; no waiting forever for a hot slot. A pool allocation path outside the common lease protocol invalidates the proof.
contracts.source_capacity: At least64B actual payload per active SET parent and native callback identity are required. Existing8 heads/32 translated write-data words/other buffers remain common to all controls. A speculative prepare does not create an extra walker or a free third translation lifecycle.
contracts.cancellation_fault_semantics: Only an optional preparatory translation may have its error result dropped. Already-issued real memory errors/responses are still consumed and accounted. A demand fixed-address fault cannot be hidden by assigning an unrelated page.

critical_source_review.finding: The directly read interface exposes init, IOVA/context/access type, update/error and AXI memory ports; no ticketed cancel input/ack. Cancellation is a proposed new contract, not an existing feature.

MEM_ACCESS publishes AR VALID until READY; PROC_PTE consumes the response and nonleaf normally advances back to MEM_ACCESS. Add cancellation only at an unpublished next-AR boundary, or drain the already-published AR first. No assumed long structural walker gap.

Successful leaf completion may fill IOTLB; A/D not set causes error in the current implementation rather than an architected PTE write. Optional cancel/fault terminal arbitration and fill suppression must be explicit; normal permissions remain necessary.
Existing fixed parent and decouple_aw cannot implement a mutable concrete destination. Keep the new SET/pool parent and stable write child introduced by round03.

hand_positive.status: A feasible normalized conditional schedule, not native cycles, not a model pass, not superiority over every early-prepare or timer policy.
hand_positive.prefix: C0 is a charged common legal prefix: A1's64B READ/WRITE/B, consumer reading/synchronization, and V's normal source64B READ/check complete before this fork. Original-start metrics are C0 plus listed times. A downstream model must allow controls to alter/overlap this prefix instead of forcibly inheriting it.
assumptions: One walker and one serial shared memory transaction server. Each PTE service costs4 normalized time units; a real64B source transfer costs AR1+R8=9; a WRITE costs AW1+W8+B1=10.
X's first two PTE services occupy0-4 and4-8. Its next PTE AR would first become visible at8 and, absent cancellation, occupies8-12.
The real consumer release/lease exchange of resident Y completes at8, having arrived at7; chosen normal Y permission lookup costs8-9. Its concrete data WRITE therefore first becomes ready at9.
Cancel drains the second PTE, adds one handover cycle8-9 and prevents the unpublished third AR. The handover overlaps mandatory Y permission lookup but is not free hardware.

A2 arrives at14, after the ordinary X prefetch would finish. Its source is cold and has3PTE services, its fixed destination Z is hot. Initial lookup14-15 and post-fill check are charged and may overlap unrelated data service; destination check adds1 serialized unit after its READ.

No future X demand occurs before invalidation/eviction in the positive branch. Y/Z remain resident long enough, or the already-granted concrete Y physical head legally preserves its chosen request. All data writes really happen.
candidate_schedule: 0-4:X PTE1;4-8:X PTE2;8-9:cancel handover + actual chosen-Y check
19-31:A2 source3PTEs;31-40:A2 AR/R8;40-41:A2 normal Z check;41-51:A2 AW/W8/B
ordinary_prepare_late_schedule: 0-4:X PTE1;4-8:X PTE2;8-12:X PTE3, optional X result discarded because allocator choseY
8-9:normal Y check overlaps X service;12-22:V AW/W8/B toY

numbers.difference: One real PTE avoided,3 elapsed units saved after priced1 handover. V and A2 both improve by3 in this conditional schedule.
numbers.total_real_data: Including common A1,3actual64B COPYs:24Rbeats,24Wbeats,3AR,3AW,3B plus consumer access/cache synchronization; candidate has5 PTE reads in this suffix versus6 for control. V/A payload and completion costs are unchanged.
numbers.limitation: C0 preparation overlap, selected output lease/check timing, service arbitration and real instruction arrival are decisive. A wait-for-Y policy can beat this one release history. This schedule alone is not a complete uncertainty/fairness result.

hand_positive.why_old_interrupt_does_not_trigger_here: The higher-priority A2 miss arrives at14, after X's third PTE would finish at12. Y's successful lookup concerns another VPN and creates no higher-priority walk. The reviewed old priority and same-address L2-hit signals therefore do not express this withdrawal event. A direct cross-address semantic cancellation wire added to ordinary prepare is an equivalent implementation, not a separate advantage.
hand_positive.minimum_next_test: Same original task/release trace with release7 versus never-release; allow all ordinary waiting deadlines and full prepare/ticket overlap. A useful expected V/A frontier or bounded service-work reduction must survive. Do not claim the conditional19/51 example defeats the oracle wait policy or full original-start controls.

adjacent_counterexamples.change: A2 is already ready before the8 response boundary.
adjacent_counterexamples.conclusion: US9542332B2's lower-priority prefetch termination can cancel X and release the walker at the same boundary. It exactly reproduces the remaining-PTE benefit. No independent priority/cancel claim follows.

adjacent_counterexamples.change: A real same-context COPY needs X soon after this window and baseline's prefetched X survives.
adjacent_counterexamples.conclusion: The cancelled path may pay a new full X walk while control hits. With3levels at4 each, saving the old1PTE but redoing3 later adds2PTE services=8 work units before metadata costs; net system work reverses. Price partial PTE-cache reuse if present instead of assuming a full restart.

adjacent_counterexamples.change: Y releases only after X has already published the last PTE AR.
adjacent_counterexamples.conclusion: That AR must complete; there is no remaining PTE service to save. Suppressing an eventual fill alone is ordinary prefetch cache admission and may lose reuse.

adjacent_counterexamples.change: No Y release, wrong context/WRITE permission, all alternatives cold or only one legal free slot.
adjacent_counterexamples.conclusion: Complete anchor X without a swap. Extra set/cancel machinery only adds cost; permissions failure still terminates the actual chosen COPY correctly.

adjacent_counterexamples.change: Cheap full prepare occurs earlier in actual idle time or waiting-for-Y already dominates jointly.
adjacent_counterexamples.conclusion: The assumed original-start timing gain disappears. This is an explicit stop/redesign condition, not a reason to force controls to inherit C0.

adjacent_counterexamples.change: A stale hot hint for Y leads to a cold Y walk after X cancellation.
adjacent_counterexamples.conclusion: At most one swap bounds self-inflicted work, but candidate can lose the completed X prefix. A read-only hint is not a grant; quantify this error region.

full_cost_reference.inherited: Round03 named L-F reference3355bits/420B atF4,N64,O98, plus>=1024B software per-slot generation,1MiB output DDR and existing payload/head/write queues. This is not net implemented area.
additional_named_fields: One cancel/result ack skid: ticket16+epoch16+frontend2+terminal_kind2+cause16+valid1=53bits.16cause is a conservative reference field, not a traced native enum width.
full_cost_reference.total: 543 additional named bits,ceil68B. Inherited3355+543=3898bits,ceil488B named fields. No claim of exact area/Fmax; bitmap could be replaced by a cheaper registered class at the same cost for controls.
not_free: Prepare path through device/context permissions and actual PTW arbitration; command routing and ticket ownership; no hidden third pending translation lifecycle.
One shared IOTLB lookup port, ordinary normal Y permission lookup, fill/cancel conflict logic, lease-exchange compare/mux and event fanout.
At least64B charged retained payload per active SET COPY, regenerated stable concrete write child, callback and normal error aggregation.
Queue packing/ECC, CDC/register bus/cache synchronization, kernel generation tables, wrapper pipelines and timestamp wrap/full-drain procedure.
Possible critical path from lease event to cancel-next-AR. A pipeline can miss the next AR cutoff and must be priced as a lost opportunity.
A legitimate reusable permission-ticket ordinary control is allowed. Do not manufacture duplicate walks/checks or expensive syscalls for it.
Prepare X issues actual PTE reads; cancelled prefix never becomes zero-cost. Optional fault/error drain, replacement pollution and useful later prefetched-X hits count for both sides.

strong_controls.name: Source preparation + ordinary late allocator + ordinary complete destination preparation
strong_controls.executable: From raw original workload, prepare source and one anchor destination using full native resources. Choose newly FREE Y before actual WRITE; permit N hit bypass and a legitimate efficient successful-prepare continuation. It can match V's binding and avoid waiting for X's result; compare only actual orphan suffix service, fill pollution and paid interfaces.

strong_controls.name: Published interruptible low-priority preparation
strong_controls.executable: Implement priority-based interruption described in US9542332B2, including drain of published AXI requests on this platform. Higher-priority A demand terminates/flushes optional X preparation; same-address cache-hit cancel is allowed. This exactly matches candidate when A arrives before a cancellable boundary.

strong_controls.name: Ordinary matching / scarce-option first / occupancy-first plus partner continuation
strong_controls.executable: Give the same registered accepted sets, FREE leases and paid resident metadata. It may bind V->Y,A2->Z with ordinary matching and use all native in-flight heads. Matching reproduces assignment and ownership exchange; it does not justify pretending the already-started cold-X suffix vanished unless its actual engine supports cancel.

strong_controls.name: Wait policies and eager permissions ahead
strong_controls.executable: Let wait-for-hot use every deadline, page-local/LIFO/RR policy, one-page write lookahead and full necessary permissions ahead; evaluate release7, late release and never release from original start. No policy is forced to issue a speculative X walk.

strong_controls.name: Generic cancel wrapper + ordinary late allocator using this same semantic witness
strong_controls.executable: Route actual Y-lease selection to an existing generic cancel engine and poison X's prepare ticket. If this is lower/equal full cost and covers the intended ability, it is the simplest implementation of the proposed integration. Its existence as an imagined wrapper is not proof of a previously published COPY-aware mechanism; the primitive cancel is already published and cannot be claimed new.

strong_controls.name: Equal resources/layout/cache/concurrency
strong_controls.executable: Spend extra named state/ports on ordinary cache entries, actual in-flight resource use, legal pinning, hugepage/page-grouped pools or permission lookahead. Test whether cheaper reachable locality removes the needed cold-X work.

primary_sources.title: System and method for performing hardware prefetch tablewalks having lowest tablewalk priority
primary_sources.actually_read: Definitions/design text lines180-208,258-260 directly opened, not only abstract.
primary_sources.coverage: Higher-priority new tablewalk flushes/terminates current low-priority hardware-prefetch walk. Pausing prevents unsafe architectural-state updates. A concurrent L2 hit can cancel a same-address speculative walk. Bare interruptible prepare/cancel is therefore old.
primary_sources.limit: The reviewed passages do not define arbitrary COPY output sets or a real alternate-buffer lease as cross-address withdrawal. This is a scope distinction, not proof of first invention or a patent legal opinion.

primary_sources.title: Processor to detect redundancy of page table walk
primary_sources.coverage: Compare page-table-prefix match and walk-cache progress; stop a redundant ongoing walk and later replay from the now-cached prefix. Cancellation and sharing prefix progress are old primitives.
primary_sources.limit: The illustrated cancellation preserves the same target translation obligation. It does not by itself substitute a different legal output address because a consumer released its lease.

primary_sources.title: CounterPoint: Using Hardware Event Counters to Refute and Refine Microarchitectural Assumptions
primary_sources.actually_read: Author17-page PDF §7.1 relevant prefetch/merging/aborted-walk paragraphs pp10-11.
primary_sources.coverage: Empirical CPU evidence includes abortable speculative walks and resources consumed by aborted walks. Speculation must not be modeled as free; merging/abort have protocol subtleties.
primary_sources.limit: This is measurement/model refinement, not evidence of a DMA output-set/lease cancellation contract.

primary_sources.title: Trail: Scalable and Low-Cost Temporal TLB Prefetching via Page-Table-Embedded Deltas
primary_sources.actually_read: Full21-page primary PDF opened;§5 and §6.1 directly read;§6.3 chain-prediction paragraphs and Table1/§7 scheduling directly viewed.
primary_sources.coverage: Per-instruction recurring page/region-delta metadata is stored in leaf-PTE blocks or an OS external table; confidence chooses prepared translations. The evaluated walkers use FCFS for demand/prefetch. Generic predicted preparation and PTE-embedded metadata are covered.
primary_sources.limit: The read mechanisms predict future fixed translation targets; they do not establish changing a COPY's actual output obligation after a real lease event. No claim that textual absence of 'cancel' proves novelty.

independent_judgments.rule: Because published priority and redundant-walk controls already terminate/replay in-flight preparation, cancellation and serving A earlier on higher-priority arrival cannot be the independent rule.
independent_judgments.capability: If actual COPY output-set ownership can safely withdraw a different address's translation obligation before its last unpublished PTE, while published priority/same-address signals do not yet trigger, it adds a concrete cross-module action. Generic matching alone cannot express that action.
independent_judgments.useful_benefit: If a legal original-start uncertainty/consumer trace retains lower V/A completion cost or total unhidden service after full prepare/wait/native-N and future-X-reuse controls, and nearest prior work does not already cover the integrated contract, it can form an independent mechanism contribution.
independent_judgments.stop: If ordinary interruptible prepare or existing generic semantic cancellation fully replicates the complete action at lower/equal cost with no uncovered contract, stop the claim. Keep the cancellation path as implementation support for root's public-prefix/late-leaf selection mechanism rather than inventing a new algorithm name.
independent_judgments.publishability: No current proof of Q2 acceptance, first invention, net area or native benefit. The candidate is concrete and falsifiable enough for a small downstream decision test; universal superiority is not required.

decisive_downstream_only: C1 legal actual A1->Y consumer release plus V source READ trace; actual pool/context and FREE timing; no injected cache snapshots.

C2 release just before one/two unpublished X PTEs, A2 demand after X's ordinary completion: compare orphan semantic cancel against published priority/same-address cancellation and all early/wait policies from raw start.
C3 move A2 arrival earlier than that boundary: confirm exact priority-control reproduction; no unique cancel benefit claim.
C4 later actual X reuse versus no reuse/invalidation: count retained useful prefetched mapping and partial PTE-cache progress. Report V/A and total data+PTE work.
C5 cancellation after firstVALID&&!READY, after AR handshake and at leaf-fill/error race: drain prior requests, suppress only optional unpublished future work, preserve actual chosen Y permissions.

C6 compose with root's public-prefix late-leaf selection only after independent cards: compare cancel+ordinary PWC/prepare and include same-context prefix proof/tags/interfaces. This agent did not duplicate that design.

actual_execution.primary_web_retrievals: Directed source review only; saved claims reflect read sections.
